extracted.intended_audience: Public housing agencies (PHAs), multifamily owners/agents, housing providers, legal advocates, and other stakeholders subject to HUD program notice requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts requirements and considerations for HUD's final rule requiring a 30-day notice before initiating eviction for nonpayment of rent in covered HUD programs, including required notice content, timing, scope, and interactions with state/local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day notification period requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs and owners must provide a 30-day notification period prior to initiating a formal judicial eviction for nonpayment of rent; HUD determined that the 30-day period best balances tenants' interests and PHAs' and multifamily owners' reliance in administering their programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD considered several alternatives (7, 10, 14 days) but concluded 30 days strikes a reasonable balance and is consistent with CARES Act provisions and other federal actions. The final rule also clarifies that PHAs and owners must not proceed with filing a formal judicial eviction if the household pays the alleged amount of rent owed within the 30-day notification period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on issuing termination notice before rent is due per lease
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs and owners must not provide tenants with a termination notice prior to the day after the rent is due according to the lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD is revising the rule to clarify this timing; the notice period begins no earlier than the day after rent is due under the lease, avoiding premature termination notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with state and local notice requirements / non-preemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The 30-day notice requirement does not preempt any state or local law that provides greater or equal protection for tenants; the 30-day notice may run consecutive to any additional state or local notice requirements if required by state or local law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD acknowledges state/local eviction and notice procedures and clarifies that this federal requirement provides a baseline and does not displace more protective state/local provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model notices and sample language (English and Spanish)
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD will draft and provide model notices and language (in English and Spanish) that PHAs and owners can include in their leases; HUD will treat the term “model” as permissive (not mandatory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on public comments HUD will supply model notices in English and Spanish. HUD also agreed to include recommended language: “before an eviction for nonpayment of rent can be filed” in specific CFR provisions to reduce ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required notice content: instructions on curing nonpayment
rubrics_metrics.description: The 30-day notice must include instructions on how tenants can cure lease violations for nonpayment of rent, specifically: information on how much back rent and arrearages the tenant owes, and information on how to pay that rent and any arrearages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD states these instructions will allow tenants to clearly understand steps to avoid termination of their lease and thereby avoid an eviction in most cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required notice content: program‑specific rent adjustment information
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must include information specific to HUD programs on how to adjust rent owed if a tenant's situation has changed (e.g., how to recertify income).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule requires that the 30-day notice include information on how tenants can recertify their income and how tenants can request a minimum rent hardship exemption or request to switch from flat rent to income-based rent, where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itemized breakdown of alleged rent owed
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD will amend relevant regulations to require an itemized breakdown by month of the alleged rent owed by the tenant, along with any other arrearages allowed by HUD and included in the lease, and the date by which the tenant must pay the amount before a formal judicial eviction can be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This responds to commenters who asked the notice to specify the particular period for which the arrears are due and to clarify how charges are applied month-to-month. HUD agreed to add specificity to 24 CFR provisions (e.g., 880.607, 884.216, 966.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of fees and arrearages in cure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged the rule to clarify that 'rent' owed does not include arrearage charges such as fines for late payments or fees (processing, attorney, pet, insurance, high-risk fees); commenters worried landlords apply payments first to fees, inflating arrears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD agreed to require an itemized breakdown by month of alleged rent and other arrearages 'allowed by HUD and included in the lease,' which provides greater specificity about what must be listed; this addresses concerns about how non-rent charges are treated in cure calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodations information (recommended, not mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged HUD to require the notice include information on tenants' right to request reasonable accommodations and how to make that request (including a point of contact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD did not adopt a requirement to include reasonable accommodation information in the 30-day notice, but will provide guidance PHAs and owners can use, continue to encourage inclusion of such information, and remind that tenants already are notified of reasonable accommodation rights at admission and annually. HUD will not replace sample notice language with mandatory text similar to HUD Form 5380.

rubrics_metrics.name: VAWA notice requirements remain unchanged
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters asked the notice include information on tenants' rights under the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD states this rule does not change any notification requirements related to VAWA; HUD's regulations already require covered housing providers to provide the VAWA notice of rights and a self-certification form at admission, when there is an eviction/termination notice, and when there's a denial of assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim recertification and minimum rent hardship exemption information
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters asked HUD to require plain language templates that inform tenants of their rights to an interim income recertification and hardship exemption and to clarify what may qualify a family for a hardship exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule requires that the 30-day notice include information on how tenants can recertify income and request a minimum rent hardship exemption, if applicable. HUD will determine what additional guidance may be helpful to further explain recertification and hardship exemption processes. Commenters also requested reporting requirements for PHAs on hardship requests; HUD did not adopt those reporting requirements in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content: legal and rental assistance resources (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged HUD to require the notice to include local nonprofit resources, agencies and organizations that can assist with finding housing, financial assistance, and low-cost legal representation, as well as information on local right-to-counsel laws, fair housing rights, and tenant rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued including such resources would be impactful and not an administrative burden; HUD indicated interest in using research and guidance but this section does not show HUD making the inclusion mandatory—HUD may provide further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / applicability to housing cooperatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged HUD to exempt housing cooperatives; HUD clarifies only housing cooperatives receiving Section 8 PBRA assistance are subject to this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD recognizes cooperatives' unique ownership structures but states that receiving Section 8 PBRA assistance subjects cooperatives to the same basic obligations landlords hold, including requirements from this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and justification: statutory basis and evidentiary considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters challenged HUD's legal authority and evidence supporting the rule; HUD cites general rulemaking authority under 42 U.S.C. 3535 and specific authority under the U.S. Housing Act of 1937, and explains the action is narrower in scope than the CDC eviction moratorium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD acknowledges limits of eviction research and data collection but cites Census Household Pulse Survey data showing many renter households behind on rent and preliminary analysis of the Eviction Protection Grant Program (average case length ~150 days) to support the reasonableness of the 30-day notification requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility for PHAs/owners to work with tenants (repayment agreements)
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs and owners retain discretion to work with tenants on repayment plans and other measures to resolve arrears during the notice period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD frames the baseline 30-day notification as providing uniform clarity while preserving flexibility for local actors to negotiate repayment agreements and other case-specific solutions; commenters requested waivers where the 30-day period conflicts with other rules (e.g., TARs) and HUD considered operational impacts but maintained the 30-day requirement as the appropriate balance.
